utility.notes: PG&E's own electric service territory map lists ZIP codes 94010 and 94011 (Burlingame) within its territory. This is consistent with San Mateo County being uniformly PG&E territory, as already established for other San Mateo County records this session.

value.name: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy) - ECOplus (default)
value.notes: Confirmed directly via the City of Burlingame's own 'Peninsula Clean Energy' page: this CCA is San Mateo County's community choice energy program, and Burlingame residents/businesses are automatically enrolled in the ECOplus default rate (at least 50% renewable, and 100% greenhouse-gas-free as of January 2021). ECO100 (100% renewable) is available as an opt-up tier; customers may also opt out back to PG&E generation. The organization rebranded from 'Peninsula Clean Energy' to 'WestLight Energy' on July 9, 2026 (confirmed via the City of Millbrae's official announcement and WestLight Energy's own site); the Burlingame city page itself was accessed before/without reflecting this rebrand, but the product name (ECOplus) and program itself are unchanged per WestLight Energy's own site.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other PG&E-territory records in this dataset.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes Burlingame/San Mateo County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other PG&E-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

required_documents.notes: The city's Symbium page and Solar Resources page do not enumerate a specific document checklist; the dedicated 'Solar Rooftop PV' page (which search-engine synthesis suggests would have this detail) returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch this session.
